data.content:
The corpus's digital lending directions set out the NBFC's duties for its LSPs, though it does not contain a separate section on LSPs that handle borrower funds specifically.

Under the Credit Facilities Directions 2025 (para 6), the NBFC must:
- Sign a contract with the LSP that defines each party's roles, rights and obligations.
- Conduct enhanced due diligence before engaging the LSP, covering technical capability, data privacy and storage, fair conduct with borrowers, past conduct, and ability to comply with regulations.
- Periodically review the LSP's conduct against the contract and act on any deviation.
- Adopt a policy with monitoring mechanisms for loan portfolios originated through LSPs.
- Guide LSPs acting as recovery agents so they comply with the Responsible Business Conduct Directions.
- Follow the outsourcing rules (Managing Risks in Outsourcing Directions 2025) and ensure LSPs and their DLAs comply.
- Remain fully responsible and liable for all acts and omissions of the LSP, since no outsourcing agreement can dilute its obligations.

On grievance redressal (para 12), the NBFC and any LSP interfacing with borrowers must designate nodal grievance officers, and responsibility for grievance redressal stays with the NBFC. Complaint contact details must appear on the NBFC, LSP and DLA websites and in the Key Fact Statement, and unresolved complaints can go to the RBI Ombudsman route.

I did not retrieve the Managing Risks in Outsourcing Directions, so the detailed outsourcing obligations beyond para 6(6) are not covered here.

content.text:
The corpus gives the disbursal rule and the cash-recovery rule under para 10 of the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions 2025, but I could not retrieve the full text of para 10(2)–(3), which is where the direct-repayment and record-keeping language would sit, and I found no provision on pool accounts.

**What I found:**
- **Disbursal (para 10(1)):** Loans must always be disbursed into the borrower's bank account. The exceptions are disbursals under a statutory or regulatory mandate and flows of money between lenders for co-lending, and the excerpt cuts off before the rest of that list. Para 46 for gold loans adds that NBFCs should generally disburse into the borrower's account and must comply with the KYC Directions and Sections 269SS and 269T of the Income Tax Act.
- **Fees to LSPs (para 10(4)):** The NBFC must pay any fees, charges or reimbursements owed to a Lending Service Provider directly. The LSP may not collect them from the borrower.
- **Cash recovery on delinquent loans (para 10(5)):** An NBFC may recover in cash through a physical interface, and this is exempt from the direct-repayment-to-the-NBFC's-account requirement. Any such cash recovery must be reflected in full in the borrower's account on the same day, and LSP fees for it must be paid by the NBFC, not taken from the recovery proceeds.

**Reconciling the pool account:** I could not find any provision on pool accounts, so I cannot say from this corpus whether a pool arrangement is permitted. On the rules I did find, the working test is that money should reach the borrower's account on disbursal and reach the NBFC's account on repayment, with the same-day posting rule applying to cash recoveries. A pool account that holds borrower money in between would need to be checked against those rules and against the full text of para 10(2)–(3), which I did not retrieve.

content.text:
The Key Facts Statement must show the sanctioned loan amount, the interest, and the fees split into amounts payable to the NBFC and amounts payable to third parties routed through the NBFC. The net disbursed amount is the loan minus those fees, and the APR is computed on that net amount using the IRR approach with the reducing-balance method.

**Key Facts Statement presentation (RBC Directions, para 29 and Annex I):**
- Item 1 is the sanctioned loan amount. Item 5 is the total interest over the tenor, at the rate prevailing on the sanction date.
- Item 6 lists fees and charges in two lines: 6A payable to the NBFC, and 6B payable to a third party routed through the NBFC. Where a charge cannot be determined before sanction, an upper ceiling may be shown.
- Item 7 is the net disbursed amount, computed as 1 minus 6.
- Item 8 is the total amount payable by the borrower, computed as 1 plus 5.
- Item 9 is the APR, shown as an effective annualised rate.
- Annex I also asks for processing, insurance and valuation fees and any other charges, shown net of taxes such as GST if the NBFC chooses.

**Worked example in the Directions:** a ₹20,000 loan with ₹3,274 total interest and ₹400 of fees gives a net disbursed amount of ₹19,600, a total repayable of ₹23,274, and an APR of 17.07%. The APR is computed on the net disbursed amount, not the sanctioned amount.

**LSP fees:** under the Credit Facilities Directions (para 10(4)), any fees, charges or reimbursements payable to a lending service provider must be paid directly by the NBFC. The LSP may not collect them separately from the borrower.

10. Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
(1) Disbursement of loan by an NBFC shall always be made into the bank account
of the borrower except for disbursals covered exclusively under statutory or
regulatory mandate (of the Reserve Bank or of any other regulator), flow of
money between lenders for co-lending transactions and disbursals for specific
end use, provided the loan is disbursed directly into the bank account of the
end-beneficiary. An NBFC shall ensure that in no case, disbursal is made to a
third-party account, including the accounts of LSP, except as provided for in
this Chapter on ‘Digital Lending’.
Provided that advances against salary, where the loan is disbursed directly to
the bank account of the borrower, but the repayment is from the corporate
employer, can be allowed subject to the condition that the loan is repaid by the
corporate employer by deducting the amount from the borrower’s salary.
However, it must be ensured that LSPs do not have any control over the flow
of funds directly or indirectly in such transactions and that repayment is directly
from the bank account of the employer to the NBFC.
Note: Co-lending arrangements shall be governed by the Reserve Bank of
India (Non- Banking Financial Companies – Transfer and Distribution of Credit
Risk) Directions, 2025, subject to the condition that no third party other than
the lenders in a co-lending transaction shall have direct or indirect control over
the flow of funds at any point of time.
(2) An NBFC shall ensure that all loan servicing, repayment, etc. is executed by
the borrower directly in the NBFC’s bank account without any pass-through
account/ pool account of any third party, including the accounts of LSP.
(3) The flow of funds between the bank accounts of the borrower and the NBFC
shall not be controlled either directly or indirectly by a third-party, including the
LSP.

terms of the contractual agreement and shall take appropriate action in the
event of any deviation therefrom.

for the loan portfolios originated with the support of LSPs.
(5) An NBFC shall impart necessary guidance to LSP acting as a recovery agent,
to discharge their duties responsibly and ensure that LSP complies with the
applicable instructions under Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial
Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, and other
relevant instructions as issued from time to time.

specified under Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies –

NBFC with an LSP shall in no manner dilute or absolve the NBFC of its
obligations under any statutory or regulatory provision, and the NBFC shall
remain fully responsible and liable for all acts and omissions of the LSP.

12. Grievance redressal
(1) An NBFC, and their LSP which has an interface with the borrower, shall
designate nodal grievance redressal officers to deal with digital lending related
complaints/ issues raised by the borrower.
(2) Contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officers shall be prominently
displayed on the websites of the NBFC, its LSP and on the DLA, as well as in
the KFS provided to the borrower.
(3) The facility of lodging complaint shall also be made available on the DLA and
on the website as stated above. It is reiterated that responsibility of grievance
redressal shall continue to remain with the NBFC.
(4) If any complaint lodged by the borrower against the NBFC or the LSP engaged
by the NBFC is rejected wholly or partly by the NBFC, or the borrower is not
satisfied with the reply; or the borrower has not received any reply within 30
days of receipt of complaint by the NBFC, the said borrower can lodge a
complaint over the Complaint Management System (CMS -
https://cms.rbi.org.in/) portal under the Reserve Bank-Integrated Ombudsman
Scheme (as applicable) or send a physical complaint to “Centralised Receipt
and Processing Centre, 4th Floor, Reserve Bank of India, Sector -17, Central
Vista, Chandigarh - 160017” as per the grievance redressal mechanism
prescribed by the Reserve Bank. This information shall be suitably conveyed
to the borrower.
